name: Korean Three-Player Mahjong
description: Korean Three-Player Mahjong is a regional three-seat adaptation of Mahjong that preserves draw-discard meld fundamentals while modifying table composition and tactical pacing for one fewer player.
deck: Mahjong tile set configured for three-player regional play

history.origins: Three-player Korean table practice adapts Mahjong fundamentals to reduced-player dynamics and locally preferred flow.
timeline: Modern era: three-player adaptations documented in regional play communities.
Current: used where three-seat pacing is preferred over four-seat format.
history.cultural: It represents local adaptation of Mahjong to available player count and preferred tempo.

rules.objective: Complete a legal winning hand under the active three-player Korean profile.
rules.gameplay: Players draw and discard in turn. Legal meld claims and completion conditions follow table profile constraints. A hand is won when structural completion and profile-specific scoring validity are satisfied.
keyRules: Turn rhythm remains draw then discard.

strategy.basic: Maintain flexible waits and avoid hard-committing to narrow lines too early.
strategy.intermediate: Use reduced-player information density to improve discard prediction.
strategy.advanced: Exploit faster cycle tempo while controlling exposure risk to both opponents.
tips: Fewer opponents can accelerate hand reads but also sharpen punishment windows.
Track all visible claims closely because each opponent has larger influence.
